h1: Zakat Calculator Johor and Malaysian State Directory
cardBlurb: Malaysia operates a state-administered zakat framework where official state agencies collect obligatory contributions, process payroll deductions, and provide receipts required for federal tax rebates.
introText:
Malaysia operates a mandatory, state-administered zakat system rather than a single voluntary national pool. Every state, along with the Federal Territories, manages Islamic religious revenue through an official state Islamic religious council, known as Majlis Agama Islam Negeri, or through an assigned statutory collection agency. Whether you search for a zakat calculator Johor portal or an agency in another jurisdiction, your payments must flow directly to your designated state authority.

At ModernWallet, we see readers get wrong most often the assumption that a single national agency calculates and collects zakat across all of Malaysia. Because religious affairs fall under state jurisdiction under the Malaysian constitution, each state maintains autonomous authority over collection portals, nisab thresholds, and administrative rules. Third-party calculation tools cannot collect your payment, issue an enforceable receipt, or process tax documents.

Our general [live zakat calculator](/zakat/) provides a currency-agnostic sanity check for your baseline math, but it does not connect to any Malaysian government body or state agency. Malaysian taxpayers who want to claim statutory tax deductions must obtain official receipts directly from their state collection agency under federal tax law.

sections.heading: State Administration of Malaysian Zakat
sections.body:
Malaysian zakat collection is decentralized across thirteen states and the Federal Territories. Each state maintains exclusive constitutional authority over Islamic matters within its borders. A taxpayer residing or earning income in Johor falls under the jurisdiction of Majlis Agama Islam Negeri Johor (MAIJ), while a taxpayer in Kuala Lumpur answers to federal territory religious authorities. You cannot satisfy your religious obligation or tax rebate requirements by submitting payments to an arbitrary state agency.

The official portal of the Malaysian government maintains the verified [list of state zakat agencies](https://www.malaysia.gov.my/en/categories/aid-welfare-and-assistance/zakat/list-of-state-zakat-agencies). That directory directs taxpayers to the authorized collection authority for each territory. Using an unauthorized intermediary or an unverified online payment gateway creates the risk that your contribution will not be recognized by state religious auditors or federal tax officials.

State collection bodies publish localized annual assessments, calculate regional nisab values based on fluctuating market weights, and manage local distribution to designated beneficiary categories (asnaf). Understanding which agency controls your territory is the first step toward settling your dues accurately.

sections.heading: Authorized Zakat Agencies across Malaysian States
sections.body:
Every state designates either an internal council committee or a corporatized collection subsidiary to process funds and issue documentation. These statutory bodies manage official web portals where citizens review local payment regulations, calculate annual dues, and download contribution statements.

The authorized agencies listed in the official Malaysian government directory include:

* Johor: Majlis Agama Islam Negeri Johor (MAIJ)
* Selangor: Lembaga Zakat Selangor (LZS)
* Wilayah Persekutuan (Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Labuan): Majlis Agama Islam Wilayah Persekutuan (MAIWP)
* Kelantan: Majlis Agama Islam dan Adat Istiadat Melayu Kelantan
* Kedah: Lembaga Zakat Negeri Kedah
* Terengganu: Majlis Agama Islam dan Adat Melayu Terengganu (MAIDAM)
* Negeri Sembilan: Zakat Negeri Sembilan (MAINS)
* Melaka: Pusat Zakat Melaka
* Penang (Pulau Pinang): Zakat Pulau Pinang
* Perak: Baitulmal Majlis Agama Islam Perak (MAIAMP)
* Sabah: Majlis Ugama Islam Sabah (MUIS)
* Sarawak: Tabung Baitulmal Sarawak

Each body maintains its own computational guidelines. While core mathematical percentages remain pegged to classical Islamic jurisprudence, local deduction categories and nisab valuations reflect regional economic assessments determined by each council's Shariah committee.

sections.heading: Selangor Administration and LZS versus JAIS
sections.body:
Selangor residents searching for a zakat calculator JAIS often confuse two distinct state organizations. Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor (JAIS) serves as the state Islamic religious department. According to the stated functions on the [JAIS corporate portal](https://www.jais.gov.my/en/about-us-3/), JAIS administers Islamic family law, religious education, mosque oversight, and Shariah regulatory enforcement. JAIS does not manage zakat funds or operate a public collection counter.

Zakat assessment and collection in Selangor belong solely to Lembaga Zakat Selangor (LZS). As detailed on the [Lembaga Zakat Selangor information page](https://www.zakatselangor.com.my/en/about-us/), LZS is the dedicated corporate entity entrusted by the state religious council with managing zakat assessment, collection, and distribution. If you live or work in Selangor, you must calculate and remit your funds through LZS rather than directing inquiries to JAIS.

Confusing the administrative and enforcement arm with the revenue collection arm delays contribution processing. LZS provides an authorized web calculator and automated payment portal for Selangor taxpayers. Directing payments to JAIS accounts results in rejected transfers or unallocated deposits that fail to produce a valid collection receipt.

sections.heading: Federal Territory Operations through MAIWP and PPZ
sections.body:
Taxpayers living or working in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, or Labuan fall under the jurisdiction of Majlis Agama Islam Wilayah Persekutuan (MAIWP). MAIWP oversees Islamic religious governance within the Federal Territories. To handle revenue operations efficiently, MAIWP operates a specialized collection agency known as Pusat Pungutan Zakat (PPZ-MAIWP).

PPZ-MAIWP manages digital payment gateways, mobile counters, and the official zakat calculator Kuala Lumpur platform. Residents calculate wealth, income, savings, and gold zakat through this portal to receive immediate verification of their transactions. The agency directly deposits proceeds into MAIWP accounts for statutory welfare distribution across urban centers.

Federal Territory workers whose companies operate headquarters within Kuala Lumpur typically coordinate with PPZ-MAIWP for automated corporate payroll deductions. Using the authorized PPZ-MAIWP portal guarantees that urban residents secure compliant records for both religious compliance and subsequent tax filings.

sections.heading: Johor Guidelines and MAIJ Assessment Procedures
sections.body:
Residents of Johor assess their liability through Majlis Agama Islam Negeri Johor (MAIJ). Searching for a kalkulator zakat pendapatan Johor connects workers to MAIJ's income evaluation guidelines. Income zakat, or zakat pendapatan, applies to gross employment income, allowances, bonuses, and professional fees earned by Muslim individuals within the state.

MAIJ outlines permissible personal deductions before applying the standard two and a half percent calculation. Allowable deductions generally cover basic personal maintenance, spousal support, dependent children, medical costs for elderly parents, and mandatory retirement savings contributions. MAIJ publishes its own current nisab threshold based on the prevailing local gold price and updates it directly on its own portal, so check MAIJ's own figures rather than a generic number before you rely on one.

Once an individual's net income clears the MAIJ annual nisab, the obligation becomes payable. Johor taxpayers can complete payment through MAIJ district offices, authorized banking portals, or the official state online system. Retaining the final MAIJ transaction receipt ensures the contributor can verify compliance with state religious requirements.

sections.heading: Payroll Deductions through Potongan Gaji Berjadual
sections.body:
Many Malaysian employers offer a structured monthly salary deduction system known as Potongan Gaji Berjadual (PGB). Instead of calculating and paying a substantial annual lump sum, salaried employees can arrange for their finance or human resources department to deduct a predetermined amount directly from their monthly remuneration. The employer remits these accumulated sums directly to the employee's authorized state zakat body each month.

Financial analysis by [iMoney on income zakat and tax rebates](https://www.imoney.my/articles/zakat-income-2026-tax-rebate) explains that scheduled payroll deductions smooth personal cash flow throughout the financial year. A predictable monthly deduction prevents the budgetary strain of settling an entire year's religious obligation in December. It also ensures consistent funding for state welfare programs.

Participating in Potongan Gaji Berjadual does not alter your legal status or eligibility for statutory benefits. State collection bodies issue consolidated annual contribution statements to employees who use monthly payroll deductions. These formal statements aggregate your twelve monthly remittances into a single verified figure that mirrors the documentation provided to lump-sum contributors.

sections.heading: Section 6A3 Income Tax Rebate Mechanics
sections.body:
Under Section 6A(3) of the Malaysian Income Tax Act 1967, zakat, fitrah, and other obligatory Islamic religious payments paid to an authorized state religious authority generate a direct tax rebate. A tax rebate differs fundamentally from a standard tax relief. A tax relief reduces your total taxable income bracket before tax calculation, delivering a financial benefit equal only to your marginal tax percentage. A tax rebate reduces your calculated tax liability ringgit for ringgit.

As outlined in reporting by [iMoney](https://www.imoney.my/articles/zakat-income-2026-tax-rebate), if your calculated income tax liability stands at 3,000 Malaysian ringgit and you paid 2,500 ringgit in verified zakat during that assessment year, your final tax balance owed to the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia falls to 500 ringgit. The tax deduction provides exact dollar-for-dollar relief against your tax obligation.

Section 6A(3) applies strict statutory limitations to this rebate mechanism:

* The rebate cannot reduce your tax liability below zero ringgit.
* If you pay 4,000 ringgit in zakat but your assessed income tax liability is only 3,000 ringgit, your tax bill drops to zero.
* The Inland Revenue Board does not refund the surplus 1,000 ringgit to you.
* Unused zakat amounts cannot be carried forward to offset tax liability in future assessment years.

Zakat deducted through scheduled monthly payroll arrangements qualifies fully for this Section 6A(3) tax rebate. Taxpayers must simply retain their official annual statement to claim the credit on their electronic tax return.

sections.heading: State Receipt Requirements for Tax Validation
sections.body:
To successfully claim a Section 6A(3) tax rebate, Malaysian taxpayers must possess an official receipt issued directly by an authorized state zakat body. The Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia routinely audits claims and demands proof of payment. Only formal documentation produced by bodies such as MAIJ, LZS, PPZ-MAIWP, or other recognized state councils fulfills statutory compliance standards.

Printouts, screenshots, or calculation summaries generated by independent third-party software carry no legal validity under federal tax law. Third-party calculators lack authority to collect religious funds or confirm receipt of capital. If a taxpayer claims a rebate using an unofficial document and faces an audit, the tax authority will disallow the rebate, assess back taxes, and impose statutory penalties.

Taxpayers who pay online through banking apps or state portals must download and archive the official receipt immediately. Employers coordinating payroll deductions receive batch confirmations, but individual employees should verify that their personal tax identification number appears accurately on the annual zakat agency statement before submitting their tax returns.

sections.heading: Using Third-Party Tools as Math Sanity Checks
sections.body:
Independent calculation tools serve a practical purpose as initial estimation platforms before you commit funds through official state portals. Calculating net zakatable assets across diverse asset classes requires organizing bank balances, physical precious metals, investment portfolios, and business capital. Our [online zakat calculator](/zakat/) provides a flexible workspace where you can input asset totals against live gold and silver prices to evaluate your approximate baseline position.

If you hold complex digital assets, reviewing our breakdown on [crypto zakat calculations](/guides/zakat-on-cryptocurrency-calculator-explained/) helps clarify how volatile holdings map into broader net-wealth frameworks. When examining broader jurisprudence questions surrounding asset classes or nisab methodologies across historical legal traditions, explore our overview of [zakat calculation across madhabs](/guides/zakat-calculation-by-madhab-hanafi-shafii-shia/).

Treat external calculators purely as planning aids. Once you establish your general asset baseline and verify whether your total net wealth clears prevailing nisab thresholds, transfer your figures to your specific state portal. Finalize your actual payments exclusively through your designated state agency to secure an authorized receipt and protect your federal tax rebate.

sections.heading: Next Steps for Malaysian Taxpayers
sections.body:
Take immediate steps to confirm your regional zakat jurisdiction and organize your financial records for the current calendar year. Begin by consulting the official [directory of state zakat agencies](https://www.malaysia.gov.my/en/categories/aid-welfare-and-assistance/zakat/list-of-state-zakat-agencies) to identify the authorized body that governs your state of residence or employment.

If you receive consistent monthly employment income, contact your company's payroll department to inquire whether they support Potongan Gaji Berjadual. Setting up recurring monthly payroll deductions eliminates the risk of missing payment deadlines and spreads your cash outflows evenly across twelve months.

If you choose to make lump-sum payments instead, access the official online portal for your state body, such as MAIJ in Johor or LZS in Selangor, complete the payment transaction, and download your formal receipt immediately. Store these state-issued receipts alongside your annual tax documentation so you can claim your full Section 6A(3) ringgit-for-ringgit tax rebate when filing your annual income tax return.

faqItems.question: Does JAIS collect zakat in Selangor?
faqItems.answer: No, JAIS does not collect zakat in Selangor. Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor (JAIS) oversees Islamic family law, religious education, and regulatory enforcement. Zakat assessment, collection, and distribution in Selangor are handled exclusively by [Lembaga Zakat Selangor](https://www.zakatselangor.com.my/en/about-us/) (LZS).

faqItems.question: Which body collects zakat in Kuala Lumpur?
faqItems.answer: Zakat in Kuala Lumpur and the Federal Territories is collected by Pusat Pungutan Zakat (PPZ-MAIWP) on behalf of Majlis Agama Islam Wilayah Persekutuan (MAIWP). PPZ-MAIWP operates online portals, payment counters, and payroll deduction programs for residents of Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, and Labuan.

faqItems.question: Is zakat mandatory in Malaysia?
faqItems.answer: Yes, zakat is a mandatory religious obligation for all eligible Muslims in Malaysia who meet the nisab and haul wealth thresholds. Under Malaysia's legal structure, the administration of zakat falls under state jurisdiction, and payments must be remitted directly to the authorized state religious agency.

faqItems.question: Does zakat reduce my income tax in Malaysia?
faqItems.answer: Yes, under Section 6A(3) of the Income Tax Act 1967, zakat paid to an authorized state agency acts as a direct, ringgit-for-ringgit tax rebate against your final tax payable. The rebate is capped at your total tax liability, meaning it can reduce your tax payable to zero but will not result in a cash refund for excess zakat paid.

faqItems.question: Can I pay zakat automatically through my salary in Malaysia?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Malaysian employees can pay zakat automatically through a scheduled salary deduction program called Potongan Gaji Berjadual (PGB). Your employer deducts your chosen zakat amount directly from your monthly wages and remits it to your state zakat body, which issues an annual statement for tax filing.

faqItems.question: Can I use this site's zakat calculator instead of my state's official calculator?
faqItems.answer: No, you cannot use this site's calculator as a legal substitute for your state's official system. This site provides a general math sanity check, but it cannot collect funds or issue official receipts. To fulfill your legal obligations and claim a Malaysian income tax rebate, you must pay through your authorized state agency.
